title: Penguins
keyIdea: Penguins are birds that cannot fly. Their wings are stiff flippers, so they are excellent swimmers. The emperor penguin is the biggest, about as tall as a 6-year-old child. In the Antarctic winter, emperor penguins huddle together and take turns in the warm middle. The dad keeps the egg warm on his feet for about two months while the mum feeds at sea; then the parents take turns. Almost all penguins live in the south half of the world, and some live on warm beaches.
familyTip: Stand a book on the tops of your child's feet and ask them to shuffle across the room without dropping it. That is how an emperor dad walks with his egg, for about two months. Then measure your child against a door frame: an emperor penguin would be about as tall.

visual.caption: True or not true about penguins? Drag each card, or tap it and then tap a box.

lab.caption: Flagship lab: flap then swim, line up four penguins by height, pass an egg to dad, share a huddle and sort penguin homes.

kid: Penguins are birds, but they can not fly. Their wings are stiff, like flippers. In the sea they zoom along. Some swim faster than you can run.
The emperor penguin is the biggest penguin. It is about as tall as you. The little penguin is only as tall as a ruler.

Emperor penguins do not make a nest. The mum lays one egg. The dad holds it on his feet, under a warm fold of skin. He keeps it there for about two months, in the dark and cold, with no food. The mum goes to the sea to eat. When she comes back, they take turns.

In winter storms, emperor penguins huddle close. The middle is warm and the edge is cold, so they shuffle and take turns. Most penguins live in the south of the world. Some live on ice, and some live on warm beaches.
adult: Ages 5 to 7. This supports the Year 1 aim in the National Curriculum in England to identify and name common animals, including birds, and to describe their structure. It also builds on Year 2 living things and their habitats. Key words: penguin, bird, flipper, feathers, emperor, huddle, egg, Antarctica, Southern Hemisphere.

There are 18 or so species of penguin. Emperors are the largest at about 1.1 to 1.2 metres. Little penguins are about 30 centimetres. Penguins have dense bones and stiff, flattened wings that work as flippers. Emperors can dive deeper than 500 metres. In a huddle the middle can be over 30 °C, and the birds shuffle so each one gets a turn inside.

Common mistakes: thinking penguins fly or migrate by air; thinking penguins and polar bears live together, when wild penguins live almost only in the Southern Hemisphere; thinking all penguins live on ice, when African, little and Galapagos penguins live on warmer coasts; and thinking the mother sits on the egg. For emperors the father keeps it for about 65 days.

In the lab your child flaps a penguin on the ice, then dives it into the sea. They line up four species against a 6-year-old. They pass an egg from mum to dad and wait out the winter. Then they rotate cold penguins into the middle of a huddle and sort five penguins into icy and warm homes.

practice.prompt: Penguins have wings. What do they use them for?
practice.hint: Where does a penguin move fastest: in the air or in the water?
practice.explain: Penguin wings are stiff and flat. They cannot lift the penguin into the air, but they push it fast through the water.

practice.prompt: A huddle has {n} penguins. {k} are in the warm middle. How many are on the cold edge?
practice.hint: Take the middle ones away from the whole huddle.
practice.explain: {n} − {k} = {=n-k}. So {=n-k} penguins are on the edge, waiting for their turn in the middle.

practice.prompt: Who keeps the emperor penguin egg warm all winter?
choices: Nobody: it lies on the ice
practice.hint: Emperor penguins make no nest. Whose feet?
practice.explain: The mum goes to the sea to eat. The dad holds the egg on his feet under a warm fold of skin for about two months.

practice.prompt: A little penguin is 30 cm tall. An emperor penguin is {e} cm tall. How much taller is the emperor?
practice.hint: Take the little penguin's height away from the emperor's.

practice.prompt: Do polar bears hunt penguins in the wild?
choices: No, they live at opposite ends of the world
practice.hint: Polar bears live in the north. Where do penguins live?
practice.explain: Polar bears live in the Arctic in the north. Wild penguins live in the south, so they never meet.

choices: No, but they swim very well
pool.hint: Think of the lab: what happened when the penguin flapped?
pool.explain: Penguins cannot fly. Their wings are flippers, so they are excellent swimmers.

pool.hint: It is about as tall as a 6-year-old.
pool.explain: The emperor penguin is the biggest, about 115 cm tall.

choices: To share warmth in winter storms
pool.hint: What is the weather like in the Antarctic winter?
pool.explain: The winter is freezing and windy. Standing close shares body heat, and they take turns in the warm middle.

pool.prompt: Where do almost all penguins live?
choices: The south half of the world
pool.hint: Think of Antarctica, at the bottom of the world.
pool.explain: Wild penguins live almost only in the south half of the world, from Antarctica to warm beaches.

pool.prompt: Do all penguins live on ice?
choices: No, some live on warm beaches
pool.hint: Think of the African penguin and the little penguin.
pool.explain: Some live on ice in Antarctica, but African penguins and little penguins live on warmer beaches.

pool.prompt: A dad has kept the egg on his feet for {d} days. The egg hatches at about 65 days. How many more days must he wait?
pool.hint: Take the days so far away from 65.
pool.explain: 65 − {d} = {=65-d}. He must wait about {=65-d} more days.

pool.prompt: Where does the emperor dad keep the egg?
pool.hint: There are no sticks on the ice, and the ice is freezing.
pool.explain: He balances it on his feet under a warm fold of skin, so it never touches the ice.

pool.prompt: {n} penguins are in a huddle. {k} more join. How many are in the huddle now?
pool.hint: Add the new penguins to the huddle.
pool.explain: {n} + {k} = {=n+k}. There are {=n+k} penguins in the huddle.

pool.prompt: What does the emperor mum do while the dad holds the egg?
choices: Goes to the sea to eat
pool.hint: Laying the egg made her very hungry.
pool.explain: She walks to the sea to feed, then comes back when the chick hatches. Then the parents take turns.
